newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall St boosts Euro stocks to records levels.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall St boosts Euro stocks to records levels.

text.p: Leading European share markets climbed to record levels again on Tuesday, propelled by Wall Street's seemingly unstoppable bull run, but traders forecast a correction was likely sooner or later.

By contrast, the dollar had a quiet start to the day as Japanese officials rubbed more soothing comments into the foreign exchange markets after their efforts last week to talk down the U.S. currency proved unexpectedly effective.

On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial average jumped 123.22 points or 1.72 percent to a record 7,292.75 overnight as investors gambled that the U.S. Federal Reserve would not raise interest rates at a policy meeting on May 20.
London and Paris were big beneficiaries while the German market also went to record levels, but a touch of vertigo limited the gains there.
In London, the FTSE 100 index climbed to record levels for the 11th consecutive session despite forecasts that profit taking would inevitably emerge.

By midmorning, the FTSE was up 12.7 points or 0.27 percent at 4,682.3. Since April 15, the FTSE has risen over 300 points or 10 percent as investors took a more relaxed view about inflationary pressures and rising interest rates.
Recent economic data and comments from governors of both the U.S. and British central banks have allayed market fears that interest rates might rise sharply this year.
But faced with such a rapid rise, traders believed the euphoria cannot last indefinitely.
"The trend is still up but I would still be looking for a small correction, possibly to around 4,550," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
"This market is overbought and needs to come down. All it will take is a big one-day drop on Wall Street to set things in motion," another trader said.

Markets believe that the United States is enjoying strong economic growth without the growing inflationary pressures which have accompanied past upswings. This means the Fed might not feel the need to raise rates for a second time this year on May 20.
But every week brings more U.S. economic data which can rapidly change perceptions.

This week investors are awaiting the April producer price index due on Wednesday, expected by analysts to be unchanged, and the consumer price index, forecast to be up 2.6 percent year-on-year, which is due on Thursday.
Paris had a similar story to tell to London, with the CAC 40 index of blue chips up 16.78 points or 0.62 percent at 2,709.87, albeit below the all time high set in March.
The French market has worries of its own with parliamentary elections scheduled for May 25 and June 1.
Two overnight opinion polls by Louis Harris and and BVA gave a lead to the centre-right government coalition, which investors believe to be more friendly to business than the opposition Socialists.
These polls follow a weekend Sofres study which gave the coalition a comfortable lead after a series of polls which indicated that the race would be tightly contested.
Jacques Chahine Finance forecast that if the conservatives won, the CAC could go over the 3,000 level while if the Socialists won it would fall to 2,400.
On the German markets the DAX index also climbed to record levels. But by mid morning it had slipped just below its intradday record and was up 6.02 points at 3,581.39

Prices were well below all-time highs set in non-bourse electronic trade as investors grew nervous at the dizzy levels. Deutsche Telekom slipped 84 pfennigs to 40.35 marks on profit taking after the company announced a group net profit of 1.8 billion marks ($1.1 billion), a figure which analysts said was better than expected.
On the foreign exchange markets the dollar was stable against the yen and the mark, helped by more soothing comments from Japanese officials overnight aimed at halting the recent wild market swings.
The dollar was at 119.0 yen after dipping to its lowest level in almost four months on Monday at 117.50.

"A raft of comments from Japanese officials helped stabilise the situation and I think they were genuinely taken aback by the sheer speed of the dollar's fall since last week," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America.

Japanese ministry of finance officials precipitated the biggest one-week dollar/yen fall since 1989 last week by warning the markets about possible intervention to prevent further yen weakness. This combined with talk of a Japanese interest rate rise to send the dollar into tailspin.
But earlier on Tuesay, Japanese finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said he expected foreign exchange markets to settle down soon at an appropriate level.
Against the mark, the dollar was little changed from Monday just below the psychological 1.70 level at 1.6967 compared with 1.7035 late on Monday.
STOCK PRICES AT 0900 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 12.7 points or 0.27 percent at 4,682.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 16.78 points or 0.62 percent at 2,709.87.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 6.02 points (0.17 percent) at 3,581.39.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6967 marks compared with 1.7035 late in Europe on Monday and 119.0 yen versus 118.86.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 0900 GMT
Gold was at $347.45 an ounce after closing at $348.75 in London on Monday. Silver was down four cents at $4.84. ($ = 1.705 German Marks)
